solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See 10
Wayward neighbours beg to be relieved of support

definitions.note: a verb here: to support someone with food and care

indicators.note: wayward letters stray out of their usual order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
being relieved of something means losing it, so the letters of beg are taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: Unruly people next door are begging to be let off giving any help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wayward' scrambles NEIGHBOURS once 'to be relieved of' has removed B, E and G, leaving NOURISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to feed and sustain, which is a way of supporting or keeping something going.

clue.text: In every respect, medical field one can be sure of

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital specialism
I is the Roman numeral for one
to rely on something is to be sure of it

explanation.surface: Praise for a branch of medicine that is completely dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely means wholly or completely, which is to say true in every respect.

clue.text: Fun to be had in Clarksville

indicators.note: the answer can be had, found sitting, inside the letters of the place name

explanation.surface: An advertisement promising a good time in a Tennessee town.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or a prank, as in doing something for a lark.

clue.text: Donna lost heart with guitar-playing at ceremony

indicators.note: the letters are played about with, so they are rearranged
the heart of a five-letter name is its middle letter, which goes missing

explanation.surface: A student called Donna lost her nerve while playing guitar at her degree day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost heart' drops the middle N of DONNA, leaving DONA; 'playing' then mixes DONA with GUITAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduation is the formal ceremony at which degrees are conferred.

clue.text: Heading going the opposite way now

definitions.text: Heading going the opposite way now

parts.words: Heading going the opposite way now
parts.note: a down clue runs southwards on the grid, so the compass heading pointing the other way is the one wanted

explanation.surface: Someone notices they have turned round and are now travelling back the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a down entry, read top to bottom, that is southward on a map; a heading going the opposite way is the reverse of south.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing at zero degrees points upward on a map, the reverse of the southward direction a down light runs.

clue.text: Summary record of one great work

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tome is a large, weighty book

explanation.surface: A review condenses one recording of a masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is an abstract or condensed account of a text, as well as a perfect example.

clue.text: Practice no end but turn out to be a liability

definitions.note: a noun phrase in the clue for someone who is accident-prone

indicators.note: to turn something out is to tip it over and rearrange it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Endless rehearsal can backfire and leave you more trouble than help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' looks like a deletion, but it is part of the fodder: all of PRACTICE NO END is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A person prone to mishaps is a hazard to colleagues, which is what calling them a liability means.

clue.text: A merger with Dryden criminally manipulated in-house result

indicators.note: the letters are treated criminally, bent out of their honest order

explanation.surface: A corporate merger with a man named Dryden was crookedly arranged to get the outcome wanted inside the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In-house' means in the House, a parliament: the result is an election outcome rigged by redrawing districts.
explanation.definitionFit: To gerrymander is to redraw electoral boundaries so one party wins seats in the legislature.

clue.text: It's to be expected from spies and hoped for from shop assistants

definitions.text: It's to be expected from spies
definitions.meaning: ... is the work of thwarting enemy spying, the business of secret agents
read as two words, ... is brains behind the shop ..., which customers hope assistants have

explanation.surface: A wry comparison of what we expect from secret agents and from the people who serve us in shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters read two ways: one word of spycraft, or 'counter' plus 'intelligence', a clever person behind the till.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying agencies run operations against enemy agents, which is the security trade's term; shoppers simply want sharp staff serving them.

clue.text: DJ broadcast mobile phone connection

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a phone line is a subscriber's connection, mobile or fixed

explanation.surface: A disc jockey goes on air via a mobile phone link.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ is not a disc jockey: it is the two-letter IATA code of Virgin Australia, an airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Airlines carry two-letter codes on tickets and flight numbers, and DJ is one such carrier code.

clue.text: Even ditch, I hear, is more slippery

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second, fourth and so on, are taken from the following words

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a level ditch is more slippery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a sound cue, but it is part of the letters picked: the even letters of DITCH I HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice makes surfaces treacherous underfoot, so something icier is more slippery.

clue.text: Earliest print of hospital 45 minutes after busiest time

parts.note: rushes are the first prints of film shot in a day
H is the map symbol for hospital
the last 45 minutes of an hour is three quarters of the word hour, its last three letters

explanation.surface: A first print from the hospital arrives three quarters of an hour after the peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The leaf for '45 minutes after' takes the final three of the four letters in HOUR, as 45 is three quarters of 60.
explanation.definitionFit: Rush hour is the peak of commuting traffic, the most crowded period of the day.

clue.text: What's material to the Irish — or not?

definitions.text: What's material to the Irish — or not?

parts.note: IR is an abbreviation for Irish
material evidence is relevant evidence

explanation.surface: A question about what matters to people in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: something relevant 'or not' is irrelevant, while the wordplay attaches Irish to relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrelevant means not pertinent, the negation of material in its sense of significant.

clue.text: Thrill in the midst of Sussex hilltop — at a price!

indicators.note: only the stretch in the middle of the two words that follow is kept, the outer letters dropped

parts.note: a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A view from a hill in southern England is thrilling, but costly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at a price' splits: 'at' is a link, while 'a' and 'price' supply their own letters. Sussex is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhilarate someone is to excite or thrill them.

clue.text: Band tell tales; isn't that the manager's job?

parts.note: a team is a band of people working together
a suspect who talks tells tales to the police

explanation.surface: A pop group gossiping, and someone asks whether that should be left to whoever runs them.
explanation.definitionFit: A football manager gives the players a pep talk before a match, so that is the manager's role.

clue.text: Spad and senorita leave nest behind for risky migration

indicators.note: a risky arrangement is an unsafe, haphazard one, signalling a rearrangement
with behind, to leave something behind is to drop it, so the letters of nest are not used
completes the phrase leave behind, so those letters are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A political adviser and a Spanish lady quit home for a perilous journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'risky' mixes SPAD and SENORITA once 'leave nest behind' removes N, E, S, T. A spad is a UK special adviser to a minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a scattering of a people away from their homeland, a mass movement or migration.

clue.text: See 16
Bounder perpetually given permission to stick around

indicators.note: the permission word sticks around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: let means permission, as in without let or hindrance
ever means always

explanation.surface: A cad is permanently allowed to hang about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like a cad; here it is something that bounds, a young hare.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare, an animal that moves by leaping or bounding.

clue.text: Breaking up movement that supports Delaware's adoption of 40% limit

indicators.note: in an across answer the supporting piece comes after the one it holds up

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Delaware

indicators.note: adopting something means taking it in, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a motion is a movement

indicators.note: two letters out of five is forty percent of the word

explanation.surface: A political movement backing a US state's acceptance of a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: '40%' means two of the five letters of 'limit'. In an across answer, the piece that 'supports' another comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolition is the destruction of a building, its being broken up and pulled down.

clue.text: Shakespeare suffering; he's got what Iago had!

parts.note: ill means sick or suffering
Will is Shakespeare's first name

explanation.surface: The Bard himself is unwell and has caught his villain's malice.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is driven by malice and spite towards Othello, the hostility that ill will names.

clue.text: Enraptured by adviser, he starts raving

indicators.note: raving means wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the start of the word he is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An adviser enthralls someone who then starts ranting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raving' mixes ADVISER with H, the start of 'he'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravished can mean filled with delight, carried away with joy, which is what enraptured means.

clue.text: See 25
Get to the bottom of what's in Anusol very quickly

indicators.note: what is inside the following words, the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A haemorrhoid cream acting fast on your bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Anusol is a British haemorrhoid treatment, which makes 'bottom' a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a mystery is to get to the bottom of it, an idiom for working it out.

clue.text: Magazine to go halves on holiday villa

parts.note: Time is a weekly news magazine
to go halves is to share the cost

explanation.surface: A magazine proposes splitting the cost of a holiday home.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeshare is a holiday property owned jointly, each owner using it for set weeks.

clue.text: Name the former Mrs Trump, keeper of Republican peace

indicators.note: a keeper holds something within, so these letters enclose the next one

parts.note: Ivana Trump was Donald Trump's first wife

explanation.surface: A request to name Trump's ex-wife, who keeps the party calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect peace and freedom from desire.

clue.text: Worship of false god, perhaps, one starts to sense

parts.note: an idol is an example of a false god
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the starts of the word are its opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: Someone begins to sense that worshipping a false deity is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to admire them excessively, treating them as an object of worship.

clue.text: Treble lattes ordered for work area

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A café order of three coffees for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like coffee being ordered, but it rearranges TREBLE LATTES.
explanation.definitionFit: A board on trestles makes a temporary table, a common surface for working on.
